description: We’re looking for teammates with skills or interests in Python, AI tools, data analysis, data visualization, physics, astrophysics, astronomy, and scientific research for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026: “Abandoned but Not Forgotten.” We need curious person who can research reliable sources, analyze  data, and help create an engaging, scientifically accurate project.
summary: Pratidhwani is an interactive exhibit about eight spacecraft and programs that have contributed to our understanding of the Universe of which we are a part. This website is an attempt to preserve the memory of these missions.
details:
It is aimed at teaching school-age space enthusiasts and curious minds of all ages about human ingenuity and innovation and to seed curiosity. Young explorers face challenges such as lengthy technical research papers with no entry point and information presented without narrative or emotion.

Thus, a first-person narrative is used and a gamified approach involving the principle of "active learning" is emphasized by following up the reading with a quiz and questions to ponder. To make the website friendly, a cute astronaut mascot, Ananta (meaning infinity, representing the knowledge out there to be assimilated) guides the user through their journey among the stars.

To ensure ease-of-use and accessibility, a dictionary API is utilized to provide definitions within the website itself, eliminating the need for users to navigate away from the exhibit, where new words encountered like 'reconnaissance' or 'rendezvous' are defined by the mascot.

The website itself is developed mainly using the Flask library of Python, Bootstrap and obviously HTML and CSS, with some help from various SI tools. Music and SFX have been obtained from royalty-free sources. All the images used are from NASA's official website.
